title: Return -1 instead of NumberFormatException when WhatsNewAppVersionUtils major/minor digits overflow Int
acceptanceCriteria: versionNameToInt("2147483648.1") returns -1 instead of throwing NumberFormatException; before the fix the new overflow test for this input fails with java.lang.AssertionError at its own test method because runCatching captures the exception and the -1 assertion compares against a null result.
versionNameToInt("1.2147483648") returns -1 instead of throwing NumberFormatException; before the fix the new overflow test for this input fails with java.lang.AssertionError at its own test method.
Preserved behavior for a valid version name: the new test asserts versionNameToInt("14.1.2") == 141, unchanged from the current implementation.
Preserved behavior for an invalid version name: the new test asserts versionNameToInt("alpha-222") == -1, unchanged from the current implementation.
nonGoals: Do not change the version-matching rule: the first Regex("(\\d+\\.)(\\d+)") match is still used and the matched digits are still concatenated by removing the dot.
Do not change the failure return contract for unparsable input beyond the Int-range guard: no match still returns -1, and no new exception type or logging is introduced.
Do not change the public signature versionNameToInt(appVersion: String): Int.
Do not modify the existing libs/fluxc/src/test/java/org/wordpress/android/fluxc/utils/WhatsNewAppVersionUtilsTest.kt or any other existing test.
Do not add resources, dependencies, Gradle or build configuration changes, or unrelated refactors.
No device or instrumentation tests; no lint task; no documentation changes beyond the sealed plan; no git push.
testPolicyReason: The behavior change is only observable through a focused unit test that feeds an Int-overflowing major/minor version and asserts -1 instead of an exception, so RED evidence is required.
